_comment: Hand-curated names and notes for what the game leaves numbered. Never generated. `kinds` names the block kinds, which the lattice's style values and the records' kind word share. `types` names what stands on a face: `by` names the field whose value tells a type's variants apart, each with its own name and, where it has one, colour and points; `facing` names the field that holds the way a thing points, as quarter turns on its face; `state` names the field that says whether a device a switch toggles starts on; and `points` is what collecting one scores. On a kind or a type, `hazard` marks one that can cost the ball its life, and `fields` says what a raw field holds, by its number, where that is settled; a `facing` or `state` field is named by its key. `levels` is keyed by pack path and index; a level's `score` is the most it scores where the disc holds more than can be collected, and its note says what is out of reach. Any entry may carry `releases`, a release's own `note`, `score` or `points` under that release's id, read in place of the entry's own under it, a `null` taking a score away.

1.name: Fire block
1.note: A block whose every face is fire. Touching it swells the ball until it burns or reaches cooler ground.

2.name: Ice block
2.note: A block the ball slides across without stopping until it reaches a normal square or the edge.

3.name: Invisible block
3.note: A block that cannot be seen until the ball is close, or on some levels only from far away. Sunglasses reveal it for a while.

4.name: Acid block
4.note: A green block painted with an acid splat, found only on the object catalogue level. Touching it melts the ball.

5.name: Moving platform
5.note: A platform that travels back and forth along a straight run, stopping briefly at each end.

6.name: Crumbling block
6.note: A block that disappears once rolled onto, leaving time for one move.

7.name: Vanishing block
7.note: A block that fades in and out of existence on a cycle.

8.name: Laser
8.note: A laser beam between two blocks. It burns the ball on touch. A switch of the same colour turns it on and off.

9.name: Level settings
9.note: Not a block but the level's settings, kept where a block would be, often on an empty cell. They say whether the level is a hidden one. On a few levels they also let invisible blocks show from far away and fade as the ball comes near.

1.name: Fire
1.note: Fire on one face of an otherwise normal block, which swells the ball until it burns or reaches cooler ground.

2.name: Ice
2.note: Ice on one face of an otherwise normal block. The ball slides across it as across an ice block.

5.name: Teleporter
5.note: Rolling onto one carries the ball to another of the same colour. A switch of that colour turns them on and off.

7.name: Exit
7.note: Red until every key is collected, then green. Touching it ends the level.

8.name: Clock
8.note: A square that freezes the timer while the ball sits on it.

9.name: Switch
9.note: A button that turns every laser and teleporter of its colour on and off.

10.name: Boost button
10.note: Launches the ball three squares forward, or two forward and one up.

11.name: Moving spikes
11.note: Spikes that rise and retract in turn. They are safe to roll over when down.

12.name: Spikes
12.note: Pops the ball on touch. Jump over them.

26.name: Hidden exit
26.note: A colourless exit that appears once every key is collected. It leads to the world's hidden level.

28.name: Arrow
28.note: A square the ball can only leave in the direction the arrow points.

29.name: Start on a clock
29.note: The block and face the ball starts the level on. Here it is a clock rather than a plain square.

30.name: Start
30.note: The block and face the ball starts the level on.

31.name: Key
31.note: Collecting every key on a level opens the exit, which turns from red to green.

32.name: Lethargy pill
32.note: Slows the ball to half pace and rocks the screen for six seconds, while the timer races. That costs about fifteen extra seconds on the clock.

33.name: Bouncy pill
33.note: Makes every forward move a two-square bounce and a jump three, until the level ends.

34.name: Invincibility pill
34.note: Makes the ball invincible for fourteen seconds, flashing in colours while it lasts. No hazard harms it, and it cancels the lethargy and bouncy pills. Only on the object catalogue level, so nothing in play uses it.

35.name: Hourglass
35.note: Flips the timer, and scores more the less time is left when you take it. It scores 10 for every whole second the flipped timer shows, so 1190 with under a second left, and 200 if taken straight away with 99 left.

eu.note: Flips the timer, and scores more the less time is left when you take it. It scores 10 for every whole second the flipped timer shows, so 990 with under a second left, and nothing if taken straight away with 99 left.

jp.note: Flips the timer, and scores nothing in this release.

36.name: Gem
36.note: Blue, green or red, and worth the same whatever the colour.

37.name: Coin
37.note: Three tiers, told apart by colour. Bronze is worth 250, blue 500 and gold 750.

38.name: Sunglasses
38.note: Reveals invisible blocks for a while.

42.note: A many-pointed star that turns from brown to green and back every few seconds. While brown it captures the ball on touch, and while green it can be collected for 1550. Only on the object catalogue level, so nothing in play uses it.

43.name: Fruit
43.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

44.name: Fruit
44.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

45.name: Fruit
45.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

46.name: Fruit
46.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

47.name: Fruit
47.note: Apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry come round in turn. Collecting all five earns a bonus level.

50.name: Captivator, slow
50.note: A spiked star that captures the ball on touch. It is the thinner one, with three long points. It travels the space it has and turns back at any wall or object in its way.

51.name: Rolling stone
51.note: A grey cylinder that rolls slowly round a set course and captures the ball on touch. It can be jumped over.

52.name: Captivator, quick
52.note: A spiked star that captures the ball on touch. It is the fuller one, with four short points. It slides back and forth over a fixed stretch, as if on a spring.

53.name: Captivator, wandering
53.note: A blue hexagonal ball that captures yours on touch. It shakes, then moves one square, and the way it shakes gives away where it is going. Its walk looks random, but it starts out the same way every time the level begins.

56.name: Captivator, bouncing
56.note: A corkscrew that bounces up and down and captures the ball on touch. Roll under it when it is up, and jump it when it is down.

/HIRO/HIRO.PAK#19.note: The training level the Japanese release lists as Lesson on its main menu, with most of what the game has laid out on one floor. This release keeps it in the game but off the menu, and the PAL disc has a copy of the developers' catalogue here instead.

eu.note: A tenth copy of the developers' object catalogue. The US and Japanese discs have the training level here instead, the one the Japanese menu lists as Lesson. Nothing in the game leads to this copy.

jp.note: The training level this release lists as Lesson on its main menu, with most of what the game has laid out on one floor. The US release keeps it in the game but off the menu, and the PAL disc has a copy of the developers' catalogue here instead.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#15.note: The level holds 3500 more points, in the twelve coins on the corners of the lowest ring. They and the four gems inside that ring cannot both be had, and the gems score more. The Japanese release removes the coins.

jp.note: This release took the twelve coins off the corners of the lowest ring. They could not be had together with the four gems inside it, so everything here can be collected.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#18.note: The best run takes the coin under the exit block and leaves one of the ten crumbling blocks standing, the 50 more points the level holds. The Japanese release removes that coin and the lowest crumbling block.

jp.note: This release removes the coin under the exit block and the lowest of the ten crumbling blocks, so everything here can be collected.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in world after world, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/HILLS/HILLSFI.PAK#0.note: The PAL release put a fruit on this level, the only one anywhere in the Final. The US and Japanese releases removed it, which left the blue teleporter two blocks away with nothing to reach.

eu.note: The Final has no other fruit, but this release has one here, two blocks from the blue teleporter. The US and Japanese releases took it out.

/INCA/INCA.PAK#9.note: The level holds 100 more points, two crumbling blocks that cannot be reached.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#7.note: The level holds 150 more points, three crumbling blocks on the top level that cannot be broken by any means.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#15.note: The Japanese release redesigned this level, taking out the ring of blocks that carries two gems and four coins among six moving spikes. This is the layout of the US and PAL releases.

jp.note: This release took out the ring of thirteen blocks that carried two gems and four coins among six moving spikes.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#16.note: The level holds 4475 more points, in the gem and two gold coins on whichever end block is reached last. A bonus level ends the moment its last block is touched, so nothing on that block can be collected. The Japanese release puts a single gem on each end instead.

jp.note: This release puts a single blue gem on each end block, facing outwards on three of them and to the side on the fourth, in place of the two coins, two pills and the gem beneath that the block carries in the other releases.

/FIELD/FIELD.PAK#18.note: The Japanese release took the coin under the exit block and the two moving platforms out of this level. Once the exit is open the boost button lands the ball on the exit, and the platforms are the way to that coin.

jp.note: This release took out the coin under the exit block and the two moving platforms that helped reach it.

/ATLANT/ATLANT.PAK#3.note: The level holds 50 more points, a crumbling block that is out of reach.

/ATLANT/ATLANT.PAK#11.note: The level holds 750 more points, in a gold coin that cannot be reached, inside one of the rings. The Japanese release removes it.

jp.note: This release removes the gold coin that could not be reached, inside one of the rings, so everything here can be collected.

/ATLANT/ATLANT.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue, with one of nearly every object in the game laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in world after world, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/HAZE/HAZEFI.PAK#1.note: The level holds 30500 more points. That is ten of the eleven gems on the ring of twelve blocks that cannot be left once reached, and a gold coin.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#10.note: The Japanese release took the ice off one face of the solid ice block and put an arrow there. It also removed the blue coin on that block, which this release lets you collect.

jp.note: This release turns the block the blue coin stood on from solid ice into an ordinary block iced on five faces, with an arrow on the sixth. It also removes the coin, which can be collected in the other releases.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#11.note: The hidden exit at 14,19,18 stands on a block that cannot be reached once it has appeared. The PAL release left it out, and the Japanese release moved it to LEVEL 134, so that release alone lets every hidden level be played.

eu.note: This release has no hidden exit here, and none in Hell either, so HIDDEN 9 and HIDDEN 10 cannot be reached. The US release has one at 14,19,18, on a block that cannot be reached once it has appeared.

jp.note: This release has no hidden exit here and puts Mars's on LEVEL 134 instead, so every hidden level can be played. The US release has one at 14,19,18, on a block that cannot be reached once it has appeared.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#12.note: The Japanese release moved one of the two gems on the fire blocks onto an ordinary block, and made it green.

jp.note: This release moved one of the two gems that stood on fire blocks onto an ordinary block, and made it green.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#13.note: The Japanese release moved Mars's hidden exit here from LEVEL 132, under a block.

jp.note: This release puts Mars's hidden exit here, under a block. The US release has it on LEVEL 132 and the PAL release nowhere.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#16.note: The level holds 8925 more points, in three gems on the outward faces of 21,13,20, 21,15,20 and 21,17,20, turned away from the rest of the level. They can be reached only on the bouncy pill, which then keeps you from collecting them. The Japanese release removes them.

jp.note: This release removes the three gems on the outward faces of 21,13,20, 21,15,20 and 21,17,20, which only the bouncy pill reaches, so everything here can be collected.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#18.note: The only hidden level with a fruit, which the Japanese release took it out. In this release the hidden exit that leads here is out of reach.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#14.note: The level holds 50 more points, one crumbling block that the best run leaves standing.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#15.note: The level holds 1000 more points, in the two coins on top of the first platform, a face that cannot be reached. The Japanese release removes them.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#17.note: The US and Japanese releases rebuilt this level, and the PAL disc has a different one in its place.
